properties.name: Fort Jay (Governors Island)
properties.note: Fort Jay begun 1794 on the Revolutionary earthworks; rebuilt 1806-1809 as the star fort and renamed Fort Columbus shortly afterwards (end year = end of the rebuilding: estimated). Outline: the LPC historic district = the island before the fill.

properties.name: Fort Columbus (Governors Island)
properties.note: The rebuilt fort (1806-1809) was known as Fort Columbus until 1904 (start year estimated: 'shortly after' the rebuilding). Castle Williams 1807-1811, South Battery 1812. Outline: the LPC historic district.

properties.name: Fort Jay (Governors Island Army post)
properties.note: Renamed Fort Jay in 1904; Army post until 1966. Outline: the whole island - its southern part is fill finished by 1912 (the terrain's land year decides when that ground exists).

properties.name: Coast Guard Support Center Governors Island
properties.note: Coast Guard base 1966-1996; sold to the public 2003, opened 2005.

properties.name: Fort Wood (Bedloe's Island)
properties.note: Eleven-point star fort begun 1806, completed 1811, named Fort Wood after the War of 1812; the statue stands on it since 1886; the Army left in two stages, 1933 and 1937.

properties.name: Fort Gibson (Ellis Island)
properties.note: Island ceded to the United States 1808; battery named Fort Gibson by the end of the War of 1812; a naval magazine until ordered torn down in April 1890. Outline estimated: the original 3.3-acre island under today's main building.

properties.name: Ellis Island immigration station
properties.note: Federal immigration station 1892-1954 (main building 1900, hospitals 1902-1909) on an island enlarged by fill from the 1890s to the 1930s (the terrain's land year decides when the ground exists). Label: the place label exists.

properties.name: Fort Hamilton
properties.note: Cornerstone 11 June 1825, the casemate fort completed 1831; still an Army post.

properties.name: Fort Tompkins and Fort Richmond (New York State works)
properties.note: Taken over by New York State in 1806, four forts ready by 1808; federal rebuilding of Fort Richmond (Battery Weed) and Fort Tompkins from 1847. A Dutch blockhouse stood here from 1663.

properties.name: Fort Wadsworth
properties.note: Named Fort Wadsworth in 1865; Navy from 1979 (headquarters of Naval Station New York); closed 1994 and passed to Gateway National Recreation Area (Coast Guard and Army Reserve remain as tenants).

properties.name: Fort at Willets Point (Camp Morgan)
properties.note: Construction began 1862; named Fort Totten in 1898. Outline: hull of the park, the Army Reserve centre and the LPC historic district, clipped to land.

properties.name: Fort Totten
properties.note: Named 1898; closed as a Regular Army post 1974 (Army Reserve, Coast Guard and the Fire Department stayed; city park since 2005).

properties.name: Fort Schuyler
properties.note: Begun 1833, dedicated 1856, garrisoned 1861; disarmed and turned over to the State in 1934.

properties.name: New York State Maritime College (Fort Schuyler)
properties.note: Site transferred to the State 1934, restored by the WPA, dedicated to the school 1938.

properties.name: Fort Tilden
properties.note: Established 1917 (Camp Rockaway Beach), built 1917-1924; decommissioned and turned over to Gateway National Recreation Area. End year 1974 estimated: the hand-over year is not in the cached article, whose infobox counts Army Reserve use to 1995.

properties.name: Fort Lafayette (Fort Diamond)
properties.note: Island fort on Hendricks Reef in the Narrows: begun during the War of 1812, completed 1822, demolished 1960 for the Brooklyn tower of the Verrazzano-Narrows Bridge. Outline: the island as drawn on the USGS The Narrows 1:24,000 sheet of 1955 (photographs 1954), +-10 m (the reef is water in today's data).

properties.name: Naval Air Station New York (Floyd Bennett Field)
properties.note: Municipal airport dedicated 1930, opened 23 May 1931; Naval Air Station New York from 2 June 1941; the Navy stopped using the field in 1970 (the cached article) and deactivated the station in 1971 - end year estimated between the two; Gateway National Recreation Area 1972, park opened 1974.

properties.name: Miller Field (Army airfield)
properties.note: Founded November 1919, completed 1921; closed as an air base 1969 (Gateway NRA).

properties.name: Naval Air Station Rockaway
properties.note: Established 1917, demolished 1930 for Jacob Riis Park. Outline estimated: today's Riis Park (the station stood on its bay side).

properties.name: New York Navy Yard (Brooklyn Navy Yard)
properties.note: 40 acres bought 7 February 1801 at the west end of Wallabout Bay; the yard grew east over fill (the terrain's land year decides when ground exists; the 25 acres of the Wallabout Market at the east end came back in 1941); decommissioned 30 June 1966.

properties.name: Brooklyn Navy Yard (industrial park)
properties.note: Sold to the city (contract December 1969); industrial park since.

properties.name: Brooklyn Naval Hospital
properties.note: Main building completed 1838; hospital closed 1948 (grounds used as a Navy annex afterwards; ruins today).

properties.name: Brooklyn Army Base (New York Port of Embarkation)
properties.note: Construction from 15 May 1918, completed September 1919; decommissioned 9 December 1966 (fully vacated 1975).

properties.name: Brooklyn Army Terminal
properties.note: Bought by the city in 1981 and let to industry.

properties.name: Naval Station New York (Stapleton home port)
properties.note: Opened 1990 under the Strategic Homeport programme, closed 1994.

properties.name: Stapleton piers (Foreign-Trade Zone No. 1)
properties.note: City piers built 1920; the first Foreign Trade Zone in the United States 1937-1942 and again after the war; most piers demolished by the 1970s (end year estimated). Outline estimated: the later naval station.

properties.name: Halloran General Hospital (Army)
properties.note: Built 1938-1942 as a state school, used first as an Army hospital (1942-1947).

properties.name: Willowbrook State School
properties.note: Opened by the State October 1947, closed 17 September 1987; the grounds became the College of Staten Island (early 1990s).

properties.name: New York Marine Hospital (the Quarantine)
properties.note: Quarantine law of 1799; burned by local residents 1-2 September 1858. Outline estimated: a 12 ha (30 acre) circle at the later lighthouse depot in St. George - no mapped outline was traced.

properties.name: Hoffman Island quarantine station
properties.note: Artificial island made 1873 for the quarantine; Merchant Marine training station from 1938 (end year = that hand-over).

properties.name: Swinburne Island quarantine hospital
properties.note: Island heaped up from 1860, developed 1870 into the quarantine hospital; Merchant Marine training station from 1938 (end year = that hand-over).

properties.name: Seamen's Retreat / U.S. Marine Hospital (Bayley Seton)
properties.note: Opened 1 October 1831; a private hospital from 1981. Outline: the street block of today's campus.

properties.name: Sailors' Snug Harbor
properties.note: Site bought May 1831, Building C opened August 1833; home for retired seamen until 1976 (cultural centre since).

properties.name: Creedmoor Rifle Range
properties.note: National Rifle Association / National Guard range opened 21 June 1873; given up in 1907 (the State hospital followed in 1912). Outline: the hospital campus that took its ground.

properties.name: Sunnyside Yard
properties.note: Built 1903-1910 by the Pennsylvania Railroad, completed 1910 (192 acres).

properties.name: 30th Street Yard (Hudson River Railroad, New York Central)
properties.note: The Hudson River Railroad built the 30th Street Yard around 1851 (year estimated: 'around 1851'); the LIRR's West Side Yard took the ground in 1987. Outline: today's yard between 30th and 33rd Streets, Tenth and Twelfth Avenues.

properties.name: West Side Yard (John D. Caemmerer)
properties.note: Opened 1987; decked over for Hudson Yards from 2012.

properties.name: St. John's Park Freight Depot
properties.note: The park was sold in 1866; construction of the 4-acre depot began 1867 (opened 1868); demolished 1927 for the Holland Tunnel exit. Outline estimated: hull of today's street blocks of the tunnel exit plaza (Hudson, Laight, Varick, Beach streets).

properties.name: 60th Street Yard (New York Central)
properties.note: 'By 1880' river had become the New York Central's 60th Street Yard (start = that year: by then); industrial 'until the 1970s' (end year estimated: 1975); Riverside South was built on it from 1997. Outline estimated: 59th to 72nd Street between the river and Freedom Place / West End Avenue.

properties.name: Bay Ridge (65th Street) Yard
properties.note: New York, Bay Ridge and Jamaica Railroad begun November 1875, opened 23 August 1876; the Long Island Rail Road's car-float terminal.

properties.name: Coney Island Yard and Shops
properties.note: Built 1926 on the marsh of Coney Island Creek.

properties.name: 207th Street Yard
properties.note: Independent Subway yard, opened with the Eighth Avenue Line on 10 September 1932.

properties.name: Jamaica Yard
properties.note: Opened 1936 with the Queens Boulevard Line.

properties.name: Corona Yard
properties.note: Opened 1928.

properties.name: Livonia Yard
properties.note: Built 1922, opened 1923.

properties.name: Pitkin Yard
properties.note: Opened 28 November 1948 (apartment towers built over it 1972-73).

properties.name: Concourse Yard
properties.note: Built 1933 on the unbuilt eastern basin of the Jerome Park Reservoir.

properties.name: Canarsie (Rockaway Parkway) Yard
properties.note: Opened 26 October 1917.

properties.name: East New York Yard
properties.note: Portions date back to 1885 (Lexington Avenue Elevated).

properties.name: 239th Street Yard
properties.note: Opened 1916.

properties.name: East 180th Street and Unionport Yards
properties.note: The original shop building dated from 1918 (year of the yard estimated from it).

properties.name: Morris Park Shops (Long Island Rail Road)
properties.note: Opened 1 November 1889.

properties.name: Hillside Maintenance Complex (Long Island Rail Road)
properties.note: Opened 22 July 1991.

properties.name: Brooklyn Eastern District Terminal
properties.note: Organised 1906 out of Palmer's Dock (car-float yard on Kent Avenue, North 3rd to North 10th Street); operated until 1983; now Marsha P. Johnson (East River) State Park, whose outline is used.

properties.name: Harlem River Yard
properties.note: The New Haven's (Penn Central's from 1969) 96-acre Harlem River freight yard, leased by the State to Harlem River Yard Ventures in 1991 (start = the lease: the 19th-century founding year of the railroad yard is not stated in the source and was not researched). Outline estimated: the waterfront between the Robert F. Kennedy and Hell Gate bridges south of East 132nd Street.

properties.name: Elmhurst gas tanks (Newtown Holder Station)
properties.note: Two 200 ft gas holders built between 1910 and 1921; Brooklyn Union Gas began dismantling them in 1996; Elmhurst Park (2011) has the outline.

properties.name: Gas House District (Consolidated Gas works and holders)
properties.note: First gas tank at East 23rd Street and the river 1842, others followed; a district of gas works, holders and tenements cleared from 1945 for Stuyvesant Town (first building opened 1947), whose outline is used: the works themselves stood on its river side, so `paved` overstates the tenement blocks (outline estimated).

properties.name: Waterside Generating Station
properties.note: No. 1 (38th-39th Street) began operating October 1901, No. 2 (39th-40th) November 1906; decommissioned 2005 and demolished. Outline: the street blocks First Avenue - FDR Drive, 38th to 41st Street.

properties.name: East River Generating Station
properties.note: New York Edison plant at East 14th Street, operating from 23 November 1926.

properties.name: Ravenswood Generating Station
properties.note: Units 10 and 20 built 1963, unit 30 ('Big Allis') 1965.

properties.name: Charles Poletti Power Project (Astoria 6)
properties.note: Generating from 1977, shut 2010.

properties.name: Astral Oil Works (Charles Pratt, Standard Oil)
properties.note: Pratt's refinery of 1867 on the block between North 12th and North 13th Streets from First Street (Kent Avenue) to the river, at Bushwick Inlet; Standard Oil from 1874. End year estimated (the works are gone from the 1956 sheet; not researched). Outline estimated: that block and the inlet's north shore, clipped to land.

properties.name: Standard Oil (Socony, Mobil) Brooklyn refinery
properties.note: Greenpoint's Newtown Creek shore held more than fifty refineries by 1870 (start = that year: by then); Standard Oil's successors refined here until 1966 and ran a storage terminal afterwards. Outline estimated: the creek shore between Kingsland Avenue and Apollo Street north of Norman Avenue.

properties.name: Burlee Dry Dock / Staten Island Shipbuilding (Mariners Harbor)
properties.note: William Burlee opened the Mariners Harbor yard in 1903. Outline estimated: 220 m around the article's coordinates, clipped to land.

properties.name: Bethlehem Steel Staten Island shipyard
properties.note: Bought by Bethlehem Steel June 1938, closed 1959. Outline estimated (as above).

properties.name: Morse Dry Dock and Repair Company (56th Street)
properties.note: Morse Iron Works and Dry Dock Company incorporated 1900 with the yard at the foot of 56th Street (start year estimated from the incorporation); United Dry Docks 1929. Outline estimated: 200 m around the article's coordinates, clipped to land.

properties.name: Bethlehem Steel 56th Street shipyard
properties.note: Bethlehem bought the Morse yard in 1938; closed 1963. Outline estimated.

properties.name: Erie Basin dry docks (Robins Dry Dock, Todd Shipyards)
properties.note: Graving docks at Erie Basin from 1866; Todd Shipyards from 1916; the last dock was filled for the IKEA car park in 2008 (end = that year). Outline estimated: 260 m around the article's coordinates, clipped to land.

properties.name: Continental Iron Works
properties.note: Founded 1861 at the foot of West and Calyer Streets, Greenpoint (USS Monitor, 1862); liquidated 1928. Outline estimated: 110 m circle at that corner, clipped to land.

properties.name: Morgan Iron Works
properties.note: Established 1838 at Ninth Street on the East River; defunct 1907. Outline estimated: 80 m circle at the foot of East 9th Street.

properties.name: Allaire Iron Works
properties.note: Founded 1816 at 466 Cherry Street, Corlears Hook; defunct 1869. Outline estimated: 70 m circle on Cherry Street near Corlears Hook.

properties.name: Townsend-Downey Shipbuilding (Shooters Island)
properties.note: Shipyard 1898-1910 (Standard Shipbuilding bought the island in 1915; its closing year was not researched).

properties.name: Steinway & Sons factory (Steinway village)
properties.note: Steinway built a piano factory, sawmill, foundry and workers' housing here from 1870.

properties.name: Havemeyers & Elder sugar refinery
properties.note: The Havemeyers' first Williamsburg refinery opened 1856; burned and rebuilt 1882-83. Outline estimated: Kent Avenue to the river, South 6th to Grand Street (the article: west side of Kent Avenue between South 2nd and South 6th Streets).

properties.name: Domino Sugar Refinery (American Sugar Refining)
properties.note: Present complex built 1882-83; refining ended 2004 (Domino Park 2018). Outline estimated (as above).

properties.name: Charles Pfizer & Company (Brooklyn plant)
properties.note: Founded 1849 on Bartlett Street, Williamsburg; the plant closed in 2008. Outline estimated: 110 m around 630 Flushing Avenue (the plant spread over several blocks).

properties.name: Eberhard Faber Pencil Company
properties.note: Moved to Greenpoint after the fire of 30 May 1872; left for Pennsylvania 1956. Outline: the LPC historic district.

properties.name: Procter & Gamble, Port Ivory
properties.note: Soap works 1907-1991; the ground went to the Howland Hook container terminal. Outline estimated: 330 m around the article's coordinates, clipped to land.

properties.name: Kreischer brick works (Kreischerville)
properties.note: Factory built 1854, burned 1877 and rebuilt, closed 1927. Outline estimated: 150 m circle on the Arthur Kill shore at Kreischer Street.

properties.name: Kreischer clay pits
properties.note: Clay dug for the Kreischer works (1854-1927); Clay Pit Ponds State Park Preserve since 1977 has the outline (the pits were only part of it: outline estimated).

properties.name: Nassau Smelting and Refining (Tottenville)
properties.note: Plant built 1900; later Lucent Technologies' recycling works, closed 2001. Outline estimated: 200 m circle at Richmond Valley Road and Arthur Kill Road.

properties.name: Bush Terminal
properties.note: Irving T. Bush built the first six warehouses 1895-1897; piers, lofts and railroad followed from 1902 (Industry City today). Outline estimated: hull of Industry City, the South Brooklyn Marine Terminal, Sunset Industrial Park and Bush Terminal Park, clipped to land.

properties.name: Fulton Market and Fulton Fish Market
properties.note: Fulton Market opened 1822; the fish market moved to Hunts Point on 14 November 2005. Outline: the Fulton Market block and the market sheds on South Street (estimated).

properties.name: Washington Market
properties.note: Opened 1813 as the Bear Market; the produce trade moved to Hunts Point in the 1960s (end year estimated: the Hunts Point market opened 1967). Outline estimated: the block Fulton - Vesey - Washington - West Street.

properties.name: Gansevoort Market
properties.note: Open-air farmers' market from 1879 on the old freight yards; meat market later. Outline: the street block Gansevoort - Little West 12th - Washington - West Street.

properties.name: Hunts Point Terminal Produce Market
properties.note: Opened 1967.

properties.name: Hunts Point Cooperative (Meat) Market
properties.note: Opened 1974.

properties.name: New Fulton Fish Market
properties.note: Opened 14 November 2005.

properties.name: Bronx Terminal Market
properties.note: City market built October 1934 - May 1935 (opened 1 May 1935); demolished from August 2006 for the shopping centre, whose outline is used.

properties.name: Fresh Kills Landfill
properties.note: First scow April 1948; closed 2001 (Freshkills Park has the outline; the mounds grew over the decades).

properties.name: Brookfield Avenue Landfill
properties.note: Opened 1966 (trucks only); closing year 1980 estimated - not in the cached source (Brookfield Park opened 2017).

properties.name: Corona Ash Dumps
properties.note: Filled with coal ash and street sweepings from 1910 (Brooklyn Ash Removal Company); the city took the dumps in 1934 and the World's Fair grounds followed. Outline estimated: Flushing Meadows north of the Long Island Expressway.

properties.name: Pelham Bay Landfill (Tallapoosa Point)
properties.note: Landfilling on Tallapoosa Point began 1963 and ended 1978. Outline estimated: 330 m circle on the point, clipped to land.

properties.name: Pennsylvania Avenue Landfill
properties.note: Operated 1956-1979; Shirley Chisholm State Park (2019), western peninsula.

properties.name: Fountain Avenue Landfill
properties.note: Operated 1961-1985; Shirley Chisholm State Park (2019), eastern peninsula.

properties.name: Edgemere Landfill
properties.note: Operated June 1938 - 1991 (Rockaway Community Park).

properties.name: Ferry Point landfill
properties.note: Department of Sanitation landfill on the east side, 1952-1970 (golf course since 2015, whose outline is used).

properties.name: Barren Island rendering and fertilizer works
properties.note: Fish-oil, rendering and fertilizer plants and the city's garbage works, 1859-1934, on the island that became the west of Floyd Bennett Field. Outline estimated: 450 m around the article's coordinates.

properties.name: Rikers Island (city farm and ash landfill)
properties.note: Bought by the city 1884 and enlarged with ashes from 90 to 415 acres until 1943 (the terrain's land year decides when ground exists).

properties.name: Rikers Island (penitentiary and jails)
properties.note: Jail opened 1932 (penitentiary building completed 1935).

properties.name: Blackwell's Island (penitentiary, asylum, almshouse, hospitals)
properties.note: Bought by the city 19 July 1828; penitentiary opened 1830, lunatic asylum 1841, almshouse 1847, workhouse 1852, Smallpox Hospital 1856.

properties.name: Welfare Island (city hospitals)
properties.note: Renamed Welfare Island 1921 (penitentiary closed 1935); renamed Roosevelt Island 1973 and rebuilt as a residential town.

properties.name: Hart Island (potter's field, workhouse and institutions)
properties.note: Army training ground and prison camp 1864-65; bought by the city 1868, first burials 1869.

properties.name: Riverside Hospital (North Brother Island)
properties.note: Riverside Hospital moved here in 1885; the island's last institution closed in 1963.

properties.name: Randall's Island (House of Refuge, almshouse and children's hospitals)
properties.note: Almshouse opened 1845, children's hospital 1848, House of Refuge 1854; the House of Refuge closed 11 May 1935 and the island became a park (Triborough Bridge 1936).

properties.name: Wards Island (State Emigrant Refuge, City Asylum for the Insane)
properties.note: Leased December 1847 for the State Emigrant Refuge and Hospital; New York City Asylum for the Insane opened 1863.

properties.name: Manhattan State Hospital (Wards Island)
properties.note: Taken over by the State in 1899 as Manhattan State Hospital; end year estimated: the Triborough Bridge (1936) began the island's conversion to parkland.

properties.name: Manhattan Psychiatric Center
properties.note: The hospital's remaining campus (start year estimated, see Manhattan State Hospital).

properties.name: Richmond County Poor Farm
properties.note: Farm bought by Richmond County 1829.

properties.name: New York City Farm Colony
properties.note: Renamed when Staten Island joined the city (1898); closed 1975.

properties.name: Sea View Hospital
properties.note: Tuberculosis hospital planned and built 1905-1938 (administration building and pavilions 1913). Outline: the LPC historic district less the Farm Colony.

properties.name: Creedmoor State Hospital (Creedmoor Psychiatric Center)
properties.note: Farm Colony of Brooklyn State Hospital opened 1912.

properties.name: Kings County Hospital (Kings County Almshouse)
properties.note: County almshouse and hospital established 1830-31.

properties.name: Long Island State Hospital (Kingsboro Psychiatric Center)
properties.note: The Kings County Lunatic Asylum (mid-19th century) passed to the State in 1895 as Long Island State Hospital (start = the State hospital).

properties.name: Bellevue Hospital
properties.note: The city bought Belle Vue farm in 1798 for a fever hospital; almshouse and hospital followed on the site.

properties.name: Bronx State Hospital (Bronx Psychiatric Center)
properties.note: Opened 1963.

properties.name: Bronx Municipal Hospital Center (Jacobi)
properties.note: Founded 1955.

properties.name: Veterans' Hospital, Kingsbridge Road
properties.note: Opened 1922 on the grounds of the Roman Catholic Orphan Asylum.

properties.name: Freedomland U.S.A.
properties.note: Opened 19 June 1960, closed after the 1964 season; Co-op City and the Bay Plaza shopping centre took the ground. Outline estimated: today's Bay Plaza.

properties.name: Steeplechase Park
properties.note: 1897-1964 (burned 1907 and rebuilt). Outline estimated: the ballpark that stands on it.

properties.name: Luna Park
properties.note: Opened 16 May 1903; burned August 1944 and closed. Outline: Luna Park Houses, built on its ground.
